new_statements.quote: 1. Li accentu tonic es situat ordinarmen sur li vocal ante li ultim consonant. [...] crater, doctor, gallin, general, lateral; colere, farine, honore, machine, ordinari [...] linea, Austria [...] familie [...] statue [...] 2. Li finales -bil, -ic, (si it es pronunciat [ik]), -im, -ul es ínaccentuat e attrae li accentu al precendent syllabe, mem si li precedent syllabe es un de ti quar syllabes (finales atonic) [...] 3. Li finale -s del plurale e li finales -men e -um es ínaccentuat e ne have influentie al accentu del céteri parol-parte [...] 4. Paroles ne havent vocales ante li ultim consonant es accentuat sur li unesim vocale: die, deo [...]
new_statements.translation: 1. The tonic accent is ordinarily situated on the vowel before the last consonant. [...] cratEr, doctOr, gallIn, generAl, laterAl; colEre, farIne, honOre, machIne, ordinAri [...] lInea, AUstria [...] famIlie [...] stAtue [...] 2. The finals -bil, -ic (if pronounced [ik]), -im, -ul are unaccented and draw the accent onto the preceding syllable, even if the preceding syllable is one of these four (atonic finals) [...] 3. The plural final -s and the finals -men and -um are unaccented and have no influence on the accent of the rest of the word [...] 4. Words having no vowel before the last consonant are accented on the first vowel: die, deo [...]
new_statements.citation: Janotta, K. (compiler; with the collaboration of E. Pigal, A. Deminger and E. de Wahl). 1929. Complet Grammatica de Occidental. I-esim Capitul: Phonologie, C. Accentuation. Cosmoglotta (Official revue del Occidental-Union), Annu VIII, Nr 65 (10), Octobre 1929, pp. 165-167. Mauer bei Wien: Occidental-Union.
new_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File check: (18 pp., archive.org scan of Cosmoglotta Annu VIII Nr 65 (10), Octobre 1929) opened; p.3 = printed p.165 carries the header 'COMPLET GRAMMATICA DE OCCIDENTAL (1-esim continuation) / I-esim Capitul: PHONOLOGIE (Continuation) / C. Accentuation'. Both the PDF text (extracted text pp.3-4) and the companion scanned file lines 138-179) contain the quoted articles at the stated locator: '1. Li accentu tonic es situat ordinarmen sur li vocal ante li ultim consonant. In li exemples secuent li accentu es indicat per grass litteres..: crater, doctor, gallin, general, lateral; colere, farine, honore, machine, ordinari, semestre, sinistri, turbine; lauda, meuble; linea, Austria, diabolerie,…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the vowel immediately preceding the word's last consonant (so final syllable in consonant-final words like doctOr, generAl; further back in vowel-final words like farIne, lInea, famIlie, stAtue). The endings -bil, -ic, -im, -ul are atonic (stress goes to the syllable before them), and plural -s, adverbial -men and -um are ignored when locating the last consonant. Words with no vowel before the last consonant stress their first vowel (dIe, dEo). Lexical exceptions carry a written accent (bontá, café, númere, órdine).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Art. 5 (p.166): in compounds each part may bear a tonic accent; if the first (determining) part is a noun, adjective or the negative prefix ín-, it takes the primary accent and the second part a secondary one (férrovìa, ínpracticàbil); if the first part is a particle it takes no accent or a secondary accent and the second part the primary (rètrovenír, àpplicár). Art. 3: -men adverbs are quasi-compounds so -men may take a secondary accent. Haas 1956 par. 8 likewise: in compounds the principal part follows the rules, the others may receive a secondary accent.
new_statements.exceptions: Art. 6: words not conforming to the rules are written with a graphic accent (bontá, mamá, qualitá, café, idé, societé, buró, numeró, menú, cacáo, muséo, heróe; abdómin, órdine, término; céteri, númere, súper; límite, spíritu; amíc(?), sublím, parfúm; país); art. 8: the written accent may be omitted in very frequent words (amic, femina, inter, super). Haas 1956 par. 9: in fluent speech only the most important words of the phrase are stressed, and a vowel may be stressed against the rule for emphasis (un medicà, ne un medicò).
new_statements.domain_note: Normative rule for the citation form of the (constructed-language) word; stated over orthographic vowels/consonants. Haas 1956 par. 9 adds a phrase-level remark that in connected speech only the most important words carry stress.
new_statements.identity_note: occi1241 'Occidental' is a Glottolog bookkeeping languoid (family 'Bookkeeping') created for the retired ISO 639-3 code [occ], which was merged in 2007 (Change Request 2006-090) into [ile] Interlingue, glottocode inte1260. Occidental (E. de Wahl, 1922) and Interlingue (the name adopted in 1949) are the same constructed language; the sources quoted here are the same ones already The catalog should carry one entry (inte1260) and treat occi1241 as an alias, not a second language.

sources.citation: Haas, Fritz. 1956. Grammatica de Interlingue in Interlingue. Winterthur: Interlingue-Servicie. (digitalisat S. Belitzky, panix.com via the Internet Archive 2021-02-11), section ACCENTUATION par. 8-9.
sources.note: par. 8: 'Li accentu primari sta sur li vocal ante li ultim consonant, ma ne sur li quar síllabes bil, ic, im, ul..'; final -s, -men, -um do not change stress; otherwise stress the first vowel; irregular stress written with accent; compounds: main part follows the rules, others may take secondary accent. par. 9: in fluent speech only the most important words of the phrase are stressed.

sources.citation: Haas, Fritz. 1956. Grammatica de Interlingue, English translation (S. Hartwig 2009, interlingue.pbworks.com via the Internet Archive), section STRESS par. 8-9.
sources.note: 'The primary stress is on the vowel before the last consonant, but not on the four syllables bil, ic, im, ul, which take the accent on the preceding syllable..' (translation of the above).

sources.note: p.165 C. Accentuation art.1: tonic accent ordinarily on the vowel before the last consonant; art.2 finals -bil, -ic, -im, -ul atonic (stress moves to preceding syllable); art.3 plural -s and finals -men, -um do not affect stress; art.4 words with no vowel before the last consonant stress the first vowel (die, deo); art.5 compounds, primary/secondary accent; art.6 exceptions written with graphic accent (bontá, café, númere..).
